reviewer_binary_note: build/20-F020 (and build/int-20) were deleted by another agent while this review was running. The reproducer, ImgIO, oracle-asm, fuzz, sweep and lit checks had finished on build/20-F020 before that. The -2048 finding was first seen on build/20-F020 and reproduced on build/20-F020-rev, rebuilt from wt/20-F020 at 1aeafd0d2b51 (logs/20-F020-rev-build.log). The GVSoC suite ran on build/20-F020-rev. Baselines after the deletion used toolchains/port-20fix2.
reasons: llvm/lib/Target/RISCV/PULP/PULPHardwareLoops.cpp:906-911 (new substitution) combined with :922-925 (immediate range check) and :1020-1027 (Swapped) and :1103 (ADDI End, -immStart): the fix can now turn End into an immediate. The range check before the swap tests only isInt<12>(immEnd) for End. For a count-down loop (IVBump < 0), Start and End are swapped afterwards, so an End constant of -2048 becomes Start. The code then emits 'ADDI %end, -immStart' = 'ADDI %x, 2048', which is not a legal 12-bit immediate. Reproducer: logs/20-F020-review/m.ll (a do-while counting down 'icmp sgt %inc, -2048', exit phi [-2048, %loop], [%i, %entry]; valid, unguarded IR). With -verify-machineinstrs: 'Bad machine code: Invalid immediate ... %13:gpr = ADDI %3:gpr, 2048' in loop.preheader. Without the verifier (the normal clang/llc path) it compiles with no error and the assembler encodes the value as -2048 ('addi a1, a0, -0x800'), so the hardware-loop count is wrong. On GVSoC (logs/20-F020-review/mdrv.c + m_ref.ll, compared with the same IR built without xpulpv): start -3000 and -2047 give OK, then start -2000 (48 iterations expected) hangs, because the count is about 2^32. Before this change the same IR stopped with the dominance/LiveVariables error. So the change turns a loud compiler failure into a silent miscompile/hang for this input. It must not land as is. Suggested direction, for the worker to decide and justify: make the immediate range check cover both roles of both operands (for example also require isInt<12>(-immEnd) when End is an immediate and IVBump < 0, or do the check after the swap), and add this case to the GVSoC ir.ll driver. Only -2048 is affected, since checkForImmediate only recognises 'ADDI $x0, simm12' and copies of it. I could not produce this shape from C in a few tries (no hardware loop formed), so it is an IR-level hole with unconfirmed reach from C.

notes/20/F020.md 'Why this is equivalent': the claim that the substituted immediate gives 'the same thing the pass already does for loops whose bounds are immediates' does not hold for End. Before the fix, End could only be an immediate from the imm5 compare branches (range -16..15), so the -immStart path after the swap was never reached with -2048. The note should say that the change opens this new path and how it is range-checked.

verified_ok.diff_scope: One commit, +20 lines in computeCount only. Fixup subject is correct. Change-Note trailer present. No removed logic, no early returns, no test edits.
verified_ok.availability_check: Correct and complete for SSA MIR. getLoopTripCount accepts an in-loop register only if !properlyDominates(DefBB, Header). Given a (speculative) preheader that is the unique outside predecessor of the header, a block outside the loop dominates the header exactly when it dominates PH. So a def in PH itself (dominates(PH,PH) is true, and the def comes before getFirstTerminator), or in any dominator of PH, keeps its register. Only header or in-loop defs are replaced. Multiple defs: getVRegDef returns null, so the register is treated as not available and replaced (safe). Physical registers: returns true (not replaced), and getLoopTripCount already accepts only $x0. The immEnd==0 in-loop case gets a COPY $x0 in PH, which is then available. The Start substitution is effectively dead, since the IV phi's preheader input always dominates PH, but it is harmless.
verified_ok.hexagon_parity: Hexagon (llvmorg-20.1.8 HexagonHardwareLoops.cpp:743-756) replaces A2_tfrsi/A2_tfrpi registers unconditionally. The fork does it only when the register is unavailable, to keep existing code byte-identical. The difference is explained in the note and is acceptable. Hexagon's own immediate handling has no 12-bit limit, which is why the range issue above is fork-specific.
